title: Chapter 16. Yadu: Two Gaura-padas from the *Padakalpataru* Found in the Full Check of PK
html:
This chapter is the result of a full check of all four volumes of the Padakalpataru (PK) by the signatures of the poets contemporary with Mahaprabhu on Majumdar's list. Only three gaura-padas turned out to be unknown to the catalogue and to translations 01–15, all signed "Yadu" (Yadunatha): two are translated here, the third (PK 703) is in nagari-bhava and is deferred to the section of nagari-padas. The other results of the check are PK numbers for padas previously known only from the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT), the Bhakti-ratnakara or the Kshanada-gita-chintamani and already translated (YD-003 = PK 2512, YD-004 = PK 1976, AN-007 = PK 2328, AN-008 = PK 2337, BD-028 = PK 2301, BD-041 = PK 635, KR-004 = PK 1464, VG-151 = PK 2668), and a correction: Balarama's pada "saba abatāra sāra…" (chapter 13, no. 8) is PK 2201, bearing his signature in PK itself, not Lochana Dasa's pada PK 2203; the notes of those chapters have been supplemented. Both padas of this chapter stand in the 20th pallava of PK ("Sri Gaurachandra — other descriptions") and are also in GPT1 (p. 37, nos. 33–34): praise of the Gaura-avatara, before whom all living beings weep, and the love of Gaura and Gadadhara. The text follows PK with the GPT variants; the Bengali original and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Yadu — "jalera jība kānde dekhiyā pratibimba…" (PK 2209; GPT1 p. 37, no. 34)

Praise of the Gaura-avatara: at the sight of Gorachand all living beings weep — the creatures of the water seeing His reflection, the beasts and birds in the forests; trees thrill, stones melt, the blind weep aloud hearing of Him, the wives of noble families weep, the deaf and the helpless, infants leaving the breast; there will be no such incarnation again — He saved all, only the poet is left out. Raga mangala.1

জলের জীব কান্দে দেখিয়া প্রতিবিম্ব কাননে কান্দয়ে পশু পাখী ।
তরুয়া পুলকিত পাষাণ দরবিত শুনিয়া অন্ধ কান্দে ডাকি ॥

jalera jība kānde dekhiyā pratibimba kānane kāndaye paśu pākhī |
taruyā pulakita pāṣāṇa darabita śuniyā andha kānde ḍāki ||

jalera jība — the creatures of the water; kānde — weep; dekhiyā pratibimba — seeing [His] reflection; kānane — in the forest; kāndaye paśu pākhī — beasts and birds weep; taruyā pulakita — the trees thrill; pāṣāṇa darabita — the stones melt; śuniyā — hearing; andha kānde ḍāki — the blind weep, crying out

1.1The creatures of the water weep, seeing His reflection; in the forests the beasts and birds weep; the trees thrill, the stones melt, the blind, hearing of Him, weep and cry aloud.

অপরূপ গোরাচাঁদের দেহ ।
অসীম অনুভব এক মুখে কি কহব মনে যে মুখে না আইসে সেহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

aparūpa gorācām̐dera deha |
asīma anubhaba eka mukhe ki kahaba mane ye mukhe nā āise seha || dhru ||

aparūpa — wondrous; gorācām̐dera deha — the body of Gorachand; asīma anubhaba — boundless is what one feels; eka mukhe — with one mouth; ki kahaba — what shall I tell; mane ye — what is in the heart; mukhe nā āise seha — that does not come to the lips

1.2(Refrain) Wondrous is the body of Gorachand! Boundless is what one feels: how can one tell it with a single mouth? What is in the heart does not come to the lips.

কুলের কুল-বধূ ফুকরি সেহ কান্দে বধির জড় কান্দে ধান্দে ।
মায়ের স্তন ছাড়ি দুধের বালক না জানি কিবা লাগি কান্দে ॥

kulera kula-badhū phukari seha kānde badhira jaṛa kānde dhānde |
māyera stana chāṛi dudhera bālaka nā jāni kibā lāgi kānde ||

kulera kula-badhū — the wives of noble families; phukari seha kānde — even they weep aloud; badhira jaṛa — the deaf and the helpless; kānde dhānde — weep in bewilderment; māyera stana chāṛi — leaving the mother's breast; dudhera bālaka — the suckling infant; nā jāni kibā lāgi kānde — weeps, no one knows why

1.3The wives of noble families — even they weep aloud; the deaf and the helpless weep in bewilderment; the infant, leaving its mother's breast, weeps — no one knows why.2

এমন অবতার হবেক নাহি আর কেবল করুণার সিন্ধু ।
পতিত মূঢ় জড় অজড় উদ্ধারিল কেবল বঞ্চিত ভেল যদু ॥

emana abatāra habeka nāhi āra kebala karuṇāra sindhu |
patita mūṛha jaṛa ajaṛa uddhārila kebala bañcita bhela yadu ||

emana abatāra — such an incarnation; habeka nāhi āra — there will be no more; kebala karuṇāra sindhu — an ocean of nothing but mercy; patita — the fallen; mūṛha — the foolish; jaṛa ajaṛa — the inanimate and the animate; uddhārila — He saved; kebala bañcita bhela yadu — only Yadu was left out

1.4There will be no such incarnation again: He is an ocean of nothing but mercy. The fallen, the foolish, the inanimate and the animate — He saved them all; only Yadu was left out.3

2. Yadu — "gaura gadādhara duhum̐ tanu sundara…" (PK 2182; GPT1 p. 37, no. 33)

Gaura and Gadadhara: both are beautiful and wondrously spread prema; when, rejoicing, they touch each other, nectar flows; hand in hand, eye to eye — a sweetness beyond understanding; who, plunging into these feelings, will reach the bottom? Seeing them, people forget body and mind. Raga kedara.4

গৌর গদাধর দুহুঁ তনু সুন্দর অপরূপ প্রেম বিথার ।
দুহুঁ দুহুঁ হরষে পরশে যব বিলসয়ে অমিয়া বরিখে অনিবার ॥

gaura gadādhara duhum̐ tanu sundara aparūpa prema bithāra |
duhum̐ duhum̐ haraṣe paraśe yaba bilasaye amiyā barikhe anibāra ||

gaura gadādhara — Gaura and Gadadhara; duhum̐ tanu sundara — both beautiful in body; aparūpa prema bithāra — wondrously spreading prema; duhum̐ duhum̐ haraṣe — both rejoicing; paraśe yaba bilasaye — when they play, touching [each other]; amiyā barikhe anibāra — nectar pours without end

2.1Gaura and Gadadhara — both are beautiful, wondrously spreading prema;
when, rejoicing, they touch each other in their play, nectar pours without end.5

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ দুহুঁ জন-নেহ ।
কো অছু ভাব প্রেমময় চাতুরি নিমজিয়া পাওব থেহ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dekha dekha aparūpa duhum̐ jana-neha |
ko achu bhāba premamaya cāturi nimajiyā pāoba theha || dhru ||

dekha dekha — behold, behold; aparūpa — wondrous; duhum̐ jana-neha — the love of the two; ko — who; achu bhāba — [into] such feelings; premamaya cāturi — [into] an art full of prema; nimajiyā — plunging; pāoba theha — will reach the bottom

2.2(Refrain) Behold, behold: wondrous is the love of these two!
Who, plunging into these feelings, into this art full of prema, will reach the bottom?

করে করে নয়নে নয়নে যোই মাধুরি সো সব কি বুঝব হাম ।
অপরূপ রূপ হেরি তনু চমকিত অখিল ভুবনে অনুপাম ॥

kare kare nayane nayane yoi mādhuri so saba ki bujhaba hāma |
aparūpa rūpa heri tanu camakita akhila bhubane anupāma ||

kare kare — hand in hand; nayane nayane — eye to eye; yoi mādhuri — that sweetness; so saba — all that; ki bujhaba hāma — how could I understand; aparūpa rūpa heri — seeing the wondrous beauty; tanu camakita — the body thrills; akhila bhubane anupāma — matchless in all the worlds

2.3Hand in hand, eye to eye — the sweetness that is between them, how could I understand it? Seeing their wondrous beauty, the body thrills: there is none like it in all the worlds.

অমিয়া-পুতলি কিয়ে রসময় মূরতি কিয়ে দুহুঁ প্রেম-আকার ।
হেরইতে জগ-জন তনু মন ভূলয়ে যদু কিয়ে পাওব পার ॥

amiyā-putali kiye rasamaya mūrati kiye duhum̐ prema-ākāra |
heraite jaga-jana tanu mana bhūlaye yadu kiye pāoba pāra ||

amiyā-putali kiye — are they dolls of nectar; rasamaya mūrati — [or] embodiments of rasa; kiye duhum̐ prema-ākāra — or prema in two forms; heraite — seeing; jaga-jana — the people of the world; tanu mana bhūlaye — forget body and mind; yadu — Yadu; kiye pāoba pāra — will he find a limit

2.4Are they dolls of nectar, or embodiments of rasa, or is it prema itself that has taken two forms? Seeing them, the people of the world forget body and mind — will Yadu find a limit to it?6

checked against the scan (PDF p. 272, printed p. 261); GPT1 — p. 37, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 34 (mangala), checked against the scan (PDF p. 296); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 34 (p. 26). The pada is not in the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS). It was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-019): it was found in the full check of PK (the log of chapter 8 mentions it in passing — "PK 2209 — Yadu" — but it never entered the catalogue; the earlier checks of GPT1 signatures missed it because the signature "yadu" is garbled in the OCR). The signature "yadu": Yadunatha Dasa (Kavichandra), whose padas stand nearby in the same pallava (PK 2180, 2191; chapters 6 and 13), or Yadunandana — not established; C. Madhya 17: in the forests of Jharikhanda beasts and birds danced and chanted the name together with the Lord). The wives of noble families here are among all living beings: this is not the motif of townswomen captivated by Gaura's beauty (nagari-bhava) but a picture of universal prema; cf. the wives of noble families dancing in sankirtana in Balarama's pada (PK 2207, chapter 10, no. 2). "The helpless" (jaṛa) — the dull, unable to move or understand; MS P-R: "the dumb and the deaf" (mūka badhira). that exists. "Only Yadu was left out" is the usual formula of humility in signatures (cf. Balarama in PK 2201 and 2207, chapters 13 and 10): the poet speaks of himself. MS P-R-Sa: "the fallen, the foolish people" (jana for jaṛa) and "the Deliverer" (uddhāraṇa for uddhārila). pp. 250–251); GPT1 — p. 37, section of praise of the Gaura-avatara, no. 33 (kedara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 296); GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 33 (pp. 25–26). The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row YD-018) — found in the full check of PK. In PK it immediately follows Nayanananda's pada on Gaura and Gadadhara (PK 2181) and stands one after Yadunatha's pada "gaura-baraṇa tanu…" (PK 2180, chapter 13, no. 6), with which it shares theme and phrasing. The signature "yadu" is the same poet as in no. 1 (see note 1); C. lila; his whole life is service to Gaura. The intimacy of Gaura and Gadadhara is the Lord's lila with the embodiment of His internal energy: it is pure prema with nothing mundane in it, and therefore the poet sees in them "prema itself that has taken two forms" (2.4). The worship of Gaura together with Gadadhara (Gaura-Gadadhara) is accepted in Gadadhara's line; the pada has nothing to do with "gaura-nagari" (Gaura as the nagara among the women of Nadia). (nimajiyā pāoba theha PK). "Find a limit" (pāoba pāra) — "reach the shore": admiration, not complaint; cf. the humble signature of the same poet in no. 1.

✦

Notes

  1. PK — vol. 3, 20th pallava ("Śrī-Gauracandra — prakārāntara"), label "॥২৬॥২২০৯॥", raga mangala, MS P-R-Sa no. 2317 (MS P-R — 9.21),
  2. They weep not from grief but from the prema that the sight of the Lord awakens — so the stones melt and the trees thrill (cf. CC
  3. "The inanimate and the animate" (jaṛa ajaṛa) — the unmoving (the trees and stones of 1.1) and the moving: the Lord's mercy embraces all
  4. PK — vol. 3, 20th pallava, label "॥১৫॥২১৮২॥", raga kedara, MS P-R-Sa no. 2290, checked against the scan (PDF pp. 261–262, printed
  5. Gadadhara Pandita, according to Kavi Karnapura's Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (vv. 147–153), is Sri Radha appearing in the Lord's
  6. GPT1 and GPT2 read in the refrain (2.2) "who, immersed [in it], will obtain it" (majiyā pāoba seha) instead of "will reach the bottom"
